qc.notes: Every episode is ONE unbroken 8-second shot of a real, recognisable place struck by a REAL kind of natural disaster at an impossible scale. Fail the shot if the camera pans, tracks, orbits or follows the event instead of staying locked, if any cut, fade, dissolve or scene reset appears inside the shot, or if the disaster is not already at full strength in the very first frame. The disaster must be a real type (tsunami, whirlpool, hurricane, tornado, earthquake, fissure, landslide, eruption, pyroclastic flow, glacier collapse, dust storm, lightning storm): an invented event or a science-fiction element is a failure. A human-made structure of known size must stay in frame so the scale reads. Readable text, captions, subtitles, logos, watermarks and closing cards are automatic failures. Human figures, bodies, panicking crowds and close-ups of inhabited buildings being destroyed are forbidden: this channel shows physics and scale, not casualties. The geography must stay a believable version of the real place named in the plan; invented place names are a failure. Record any of these under issues.

art_style: Photoreal orbital or high-aerial documentary footage composed for vertical 9:16 at 24 fps. Preserve the named site's real coastlines, relief, rivers, ice, and city-light patterns at geographically credible scale; atmospheric effects follow the disaster shown in this episode. Render the disaster with coherent materials, gravity, illumination, motion, and cause-and-effect at a scale the real Earth could never produce. Natural motivated light, restrained documentary colour, deep space blacks, fine terrain texture, stable exposure, and legible scale cues give the image the clarity, framing and grain of real satellite and high-altitude aerial photography. A human-made structure of known size stays in frame so the scale of the event reads instantly. The frame edge is the image edge: the picture reaches every side of the frame with open sky, terrain or space, and the view is unobstructed. The camera is rigidly fixed to one position, orientation, focal length, focus distance, and exposure for the full take. Every frame maintains one continuous viewpoint and scene. Wide geography fills the image, with a final active physical state suited to a seamless loop. Diegetic environmental audio alone follows the visible event.
